_: The one look (PLAN.md Phase 2 item 1; retargeted by Mac to Warcraft III Reforged at the RTS camera: chunky readable shapes, rich saturated colour, bold house colours, crisp light). look.gd reads it. on: the switch (or --look=one); off keeps today's light. sun_elevation: degrees above the horizon (25-35: long soft shadows). sun_energy: the sun's strength (Sky3D, 1 its default; art target town-b: bright late-afternoon sun); shadow_opacity: how dark its shadows fall (1 black; town-b: soft); ambient_energy: the shade's fill. sun_color / horizon_color: the warm key (about 4000 K, late afternoon) at height and near the horizon. sky_contribution: how much of the shade's light comes from the sky (the rest is ambient_color: the cool blue fill in the shadows). lut: the one colour grade, on every view (assets/grade/v3b.png: fitted to 01-town by tools/fit_look_lut.py from Kingsmere's frames, round 8's correction composed after the earlier v3 grade; the earlier golden-hour and v3 grades are gone; empty: none). saturation, contrast: the gentle S-curve after AgX. exposure. haze_color: the warm distance haze. kit_tints: the free kit's materials re-graded by name (a multiply on their colour: earthy terracotta roofs, honey stone, darker oak, deeper leaves; kit.py's unify table). ssao / ssil: soft contact shadows (radius, intensity, power) and bounced light. haze: the volumetric haze's density near the ground (fades out as the camera pulls back) and the distance fog's density.

fill._: The fill light (look.gd; film's key-and-fill, and the fixed RTS camera of Warcraft III and Anno that always sees the lit faces): a soft light from over the camera's shoulder that turns with the camera, so the walls you look at are never left in the dark when the camera faces into the sun (batch 6: Kingsmere's street walls at luma 0.10-0.17). It casts no shadows, so the sun's shadows stay put. on: the switch. energy: its strength (the sun is sun_energy). color: its tint. elevation: degrees above the horizon. turn: degrees round from straight behind the camera (positive: from its left). Fades with the sun at night. Predicted with tools/light_probe.py.

_target_was: Foundation/Tiny Glade (storybook.png, earthy tints); kept: assets/grade/storybook.png

map_air._: look.gd _map_air_at: the air at the map's height, between from and to (camera distance; the town and army views stand under from): the sky's share of the ambient light falls to sky_contribution (its blue cast the land blue-green, g4) and the haze warms to haze_color (target 02-realm).

sea._: The sea (terrain.gd _build_sea, Boujie Water Shader). waves_fade: from and to what distance from the lens (game units) the swell settles into a flat sheen. Its lighting is per vertex on rings that coarsen away from the lens, so further out it aliased into even stripes across the water (the scanlines at mid zoom); was 40 / 120. depth_fade: from and to what distance from the lens the water's colour stops reading the depth to the sea bed (Terrain3D draws the bed in rings that coarsen away from the lens, and their edges showed as straight seams across the sea at the mid zoom); was 40 / 120.

shore._: terrain.gd _shore_code: the shallows and the surf by the land's depth under the water, the same at every zoom (WC3, AoE2: a pale turquoise rim and a soft line of foam at every shore). shallow: depth (game units) where the shallow colour has faded; shallow_colour (alpha: how much); foam: the surf's depth band; foam_colour (alpha: how white); foam_scale: the foam texture's repeats a game unit; foam_speed: how fast the surf breathes.

colours._: The sea's colours, the Boujie shader's own parameters by name (terrain.gd _build_sea): color_deep, color_shallow (alpha: how much it tints), albedo, albedo_fresnel (the glancing sheen), albedo_snell (looking down into it). Target 02-realm: a clear blue-teal open sea (about 0.27, 0.39, 0.46 in the painting) and turquoise shallows at the rocks; pass 2159 read near-navy slate (0.09, 0.27, 0.34), the old northern slate-green set (deep 0.05, 0.15, 0.2; shallow 0.09, 0.2, 0.22; albedo 0.16, 0.3, 0.34; fresnel 0.36, 0.47, 0.54; snell 0.02, 0.08, 0.12) lifted and turned bluer.
colours._g3: g3 read 0.0, 0.28, 0.54 (navy, no red) at the map zoom against 02-realm's 0.09, 0.37, 0.49: greener, less blue.

surface._: The sea's surface, the Boujie shader's parameters by name (terrain.gd _build_sea): roughness (the prefab's 0.087 mirrored the sun into a white glare), specular.

swell._: terrain.gd _shore_code: the open sea's swell where the vertex waves have settled (past from, whole at twice from, game units from the lens): two trains of light and shade from the foam texture drifting across each other. amount: how much they lighten and darken the water (0 off); scale: their repeats a game unit (smaller: longer swells); speed: their drift.

floor._: The open sea's floor past the realm's land (terrain.gd _build_sea_floor; batch 9 goldrock-30: the sky showed through the see-through water past the land's edge as a pale square panel over the sea). on: the switch. depth: its height (just under the deep sea floor's -3.2). color: its colour (the deep water reads it as deep). reach: its width (game units; the sea's far edge is 2000 from the lens).

politics._: The political map (docs/review/political-map.md; target docs/art/target/02-realm.jpg; CK3's political map mode in Warcraft III's colours). on: the switch (or --politics=on). hold: how strongly a house's land carries its colour, by its favour band (the bridge's reading): loyal heartland strong, cold land fading. stripes_below: a hold under this stripes the land in its rival's colour (the first house it's at war with): slipping. wash_near / wash_far: the colour's strength at town zoom and from far off (times hold). own_mix: how much of the house's flat colour goes over the land's own brightness (0: a hue only, 1: flat paint). border_bright: the border line in the house's own colour at full value, saturated this far toward its pure hue (0: the colour as it is, 0.95 most; g7: brightened toward white, salmon on salmon land, read as no line; g8: at full value, still pastel); border_glow: a light glow of that colour spreading just inside the line, how strong (0 none); border_px: its width in screen pixels. stripe_width: the stripes' width in tiles. map_from / map_to: the camera's height over the ground (game units; a town view stands about 5-9 up, the mid zoom about 24-27 at camera distance 40, the most the 3D view draws back about 37-44 at distance 60, where the painted overview takes over) between which the wash, the band and the stripes come in, and the plain (politics off) far wash with them; below map_from the land stays natural (about a seventh of wash_near) and only the border line shows (target 01-town: no red ground at roof height; Warcraft III: no map overlay at playing heights). line_from / line_to: the camera's height over the ground (game units) between which the border line fades in: none at roof or town height and none over the wide town shots (d30 stands about 18 up, d50 about 31: batch 9 read the line there as a loud red road), whole only at the map zoom (d60, about 38 up; past it the painted overview draws its own borders); was 9 / 22; border_bright was 1.35 (the crown's red went salmon); line_soft: the painted border's soft band, as a share of a tile from the seam; line_crisp: how much of it is the fine line over the band (the rest the band). Was 12 / 30, which coated the mid zoom's land in the house's colour (a bare brown pad round Kingsmere). band / band_strength: the house's colour strong just inside its border (band: how far in, a share of a tile; band_strength: how strong), so a house's land reads by its edge and a light tint inside (target 02-realm; pass 2159: wash_far 0.8 filled the crown's land pink, now 0.25, the edge carrying the colour; border_px 3 to 5).

team._: Team colour (team_colour.gd; Mac's North Star, docs/art/target/02-realm.jpg; Warcraft III): the kit materials whose names start with these keys take the holder's colour, by how much (roof tiles strongly, wood trim lightly; walls, brick and stone not at all). on: the switch (or --team=on / --team=off). saturation: the house colours pushed bolder (WC3's team colours). A town that changes hands eases to its new colour over a season. Art target town-b: ordinary houses keep their own roof (red tile, blue-grey slate, golden thatch, brown shingle) and the colour sits on accents: their shutters, front doors (MI_Door) and banners; only the castle, the manor, the guild hall and the armoury wear it on their roofs (house_kit tiers' 'house' roof). materials: roof tiles (the castle, the hall and any house whose roof draws 'house'), shutters (MI_Shutter, house_builder.gd), doors (MI_Door), banners strongly; the timber frame (MI_WoodTrim) barely. ranks: which components are ordinary (0 a cottage, 1 a townhouse or inn); everything else (castle, hall, banners, armour) wears the full colour. roofs: per house not built from the kit's tiers, seeded by where it stands, the share of thatch, the tiles' own terracotta, slate and the house's colour, as [thatch, terracotta, slate, house] for cottages and for townhouses (house 0: an ordinary roof never wears the colour); house_share (round 5: the castle's and the halls' roofs a bright flat red beside the houses' terracotta): the share of the house colour a roof that wears it takes over its own tiles; thatch and dark_tile (blue-grey slate) their colours (thatch: new straw, warm ochre; thatch_old: the weathered grey-brown each thatched roof leans toward by its own age); straw: how the thatch is drawn (team_colour.gdshader: bundles laid down the slope, never the tiles' rows), fibre and clump (how strongly the bundles and the patches read), eave_dark and eave_band (the ragged darker eave: how dark, how far up as a share of a storey), storey (a kit storey in the mesh's units, where the eave sits); materials: which kit materials are roofs. paint: ordinary_share, the share of the colour an ordinary house's trims and shutters take; saturation and warm, the house colour toned toward its grey and warmed (painted reds, not neon).

clarity._: With the camera's clarity on (data/camera.json clarity.on; --clarity=old for the before shot): the town seen in its true colours at its own zoom, not washed orange (Mac, 2026-11-12; art target 01-town). Over the one look's values: saturation, contrast, sun_color, haze_color (the haze's and the depth fog's light). hazeTown: the volumetric haze's share of its density at the closest zoom, rising to all of it by hazeFull (camera distance). No near blur at all; the far blur only beyond farBlurFrom camera-distances (past the town's far edge), at farBlur strength.

v3._: The v3 look (docs/review/look-gap.md; art target docs/art/target/01-town.jpg: warm, saturated, crisp light, clear air), tuned first on Kingsmere's square at the default town view (Mac, 2026-11-12: one view until it's right). --look=v3 for one run, or on; --look=one keeps the one look as it was (the before shot). Its keys are laid over the one look's above, key by key (look.gd _overlay): any key above may be set here. lut: the grade fitted offline from batch 9's Kingsmere frames to 01-town by realm/tools/fit_look_lut.py, composed after bold.png (chroma x1.15, Lab orange turned 9 deg toward the target's reds, olive grass 12 deg toward green, a gentle S of slope 1.1 round L 46, the crushed shade's toe lifted 8 L); previews in /tmp/goc-look. exposure (was 1.16): Kingsmere's square sat at L 41 against the target's 47. sun_elevation (was 38), sun_energy (was 1.3), shadow_opacity (was 0.72): a higher, stronger sun, its shadows a little crisper (not darker than this: Kingsmere's darkest tenth is already near black, L 3 vs 14). fill.energy (was 0.35): the walls facing the camera out of the sun. ssao: tighter contact shadows (radius was 1.2, power 1.6), light_affect: how much they show in sunlit areas (was 0.15). haze: the volumetric haze and depth fog thinned (was 0.003 / 0.0008); clarity.hazeTown: the haze's share at the closest zoom (was 0.2). Wide-zoom light (docs/research/quality-deep-dive.md #2: d16-30 at 0.63x the shipped games' value spread, highlights capped at p95 0.52 vs 0.68): tonemap.agx_white (Godot's 16.29) and agx_contrast (its 1.25), with the adjustment contrast and clarity.contrast at 1.0 (were 1.15 / 1.14; the docs prefer AgX's own contrast), exposure 1.35 (was 1.22, then 1.12; focus r3's close view measured mean luma 0.38 against 01-town's 0.43, p95 0.66 vs 0.79), ambient_energy 2.3 (the one look's 2.0: the shade lifted, p5 0.105 vs 0.123), shadow_opacity 0.7 (was 0.78) and ssao intensity 1.6, light_affect 0.12 (were 2.0, 0.22: the grit in sunlit areas); gi: SDFGI's bounce (on, energy, was main.gd's 0.9; y_scale 50/75/100, was 75) so less olive ground is bounced into everything; haze.fade_from / fade_to: the camera distances over which the volumetric haze thins away (were 30 / 70, so d16-30 had all of it); haze.fog at town zoom thinning to fog_far between fog_from and fog_to (main.gd held the depth fog at 0.0012 to d45 every frame, so haze.fog never took). One warm band (#10: 73% of our saturated pixels warm, 01-town 66%, shipped games 35%; separate the hues, not more saturation): sun_color, horizon_color and clarity.sun_color a paler warm key (were 1.0/0.91/0.76, 1.0/0.82/0.62, 1.0/0.94/0.86), fill.color a cool sky fill against it (was warm 1.0/0.94/0.84), clarity.haze_color a cooler, clearer haze (was 0.86/0.9/0.96), kit_tints: plaster white, not cream (was 1.08/1.04/0.96), stone grey, not honey (was 1.05/1.0/0.92). Every value an estimate until filmed. Round 8 (focus r8 hero, HUD masked, against 01-town): lut v3b.png (was v3.png), made by tools/fit_look_lut.py --over from r8's three frames: the grade is Godot's last step, so the correction measured on graded frames composes exactly after v3.png. Measured before -> predicted after (01-town): luma mean 0.479 -> 0.433 (0.431), spread 0.180 -> 0.205 (0.211), p5 0.161 -> 0.125 (0.126), p95 0.760 -> 0.785 (0.793); mean saturation 0.438 -> 0.496 (0.512); greens' value 0.554 -> 0.427 (0.369); stone's value 0.649 -> 0.516 (0.541) and share 27% -> 13% (11%); brightest 5% r-b 0.110 -> 0.206 (0.265, warm); darkest tenth b/r 0.39 -> 0.25 (0.27). Lights left as they were (the grade's effect is exact offline; a light's is not). Round 12 (Mac: the square washed out, too bright, bloomy and pale; realm/tools/still_probe.py on focus r11 c01, HUD masked, against 01-town): mean luma 0.517 vs 0.431, 7.7% of pixels over 0.92 vs 0.5%, HSL saturation 0.39 vs 0.47; the clipped pixels are warm white (snow on the ground and roofs, the awnings' white stripes, the cobbles' tops). exposure 1.25 (was 1.35) and tonemap.agx_white 8.0 (was 5.0: the highlights reached white too soon at the close view), predicted offline through the chain (AgX with its white, v3b.png) from r11: mean 0.435, clipped 1.3%, p5 0.063 (shadows not crushed), p95 0.81 (01-town 0.79); glow (main.gd's intensity 0.5, bloom 0.08: the bloom glows every pixel, a veil over the frame): intensity, bloom (share of all light that glows; 0: only the bright) and hdr_threshold (the radiance above which light glows); clarity.saturation 1.25 (the one look's clarity 1.12): colour back once the highlights leave AgX's shoulder. Round 12 (focus r12 c01, Autumn, still_probe.py): mean 0.429, clipped 0.0%, saturation 0.435 (01-town 0.470), p5 0.075, p95 0.789; clarity.saturation 1.36 (was 1.25), predicted on r12 by the same adjustment offline: saturation 0.462, mean and clipped unchanged, red channel at full 0.85% of pixels (0.41% before). Estimates until filmed; the wide zoom's highlights (why agx_white was 5) to be re-measured.

depth._: look.gd: the drawn-back views' air by depth (WC3, AoE2: the far land fades into the air, the subject stays clear): between from and to (camera distance) Godot's depth fog comes in, clear to begin camera-distances past the lens, rising (curve) to most by end; its colour the haze's (map_air warms it at the map), with the sky's through fog_aerial_perspective.

outline._: The painted line and edge light (look.gd _add_outline, scripts/outline.gdshader: a full-screen pass over depth and normals, built on EMBYR's High Quality Post Process Outline and Leo Peltola's outline & highlight, both MIT, godotshaders.com; art target 01-town's bold painted edges; the measured fine-detail gap, docs/review/look-gap.md). on: the switch (v3 only). line_color: the line's colour and strength [r, g, b, a] (warm dark brown, never black). width_near / width_far: its width in pixels at near_at / far_at (game units from the lens), gone by fade_far. depth_threshold: a depth jump of this share of the distance (summed over the 8 neighbours) draws a silhouette line; grazing and grazing_power: how much larger it must be on a surface seen edge-on (the ground at a low pitch, or it fills with lines). normal_threshold / normal_smoothing: how sharp an inward fold draws a line (a wall meeting the ground, the eave under a roof), at normal_line of the silhouette's strength. light_color: the edge light's colour and strength on outward folds (a roof's ridge, a beam's corner, trims), from convexity light_from to light_to, only within same_surface of the distance (one surface). near_soft: the line's and edge light's strength at near_at, whole again by soft_to (game units), so the close view isn't inked. Round 3 (focus r3, close view dist 6: heavy dark ink on everything, roofs and people muddy; 01-town's lines are thin, soft and warm): line_color a lighter warm brown at 0.38 (was 0.16/0.09/0.05 at 0.7), width_near 1.0 / width_far 0.7 (were 1.6 / 0.8), near_soft 0.35 to soft_to 18 (new), depth_threshold 0.05 (was 0.035: fewer lines round small props), normal_threshold 1.3 and normal_line 0.15 (were 0.9 / 0.6: the scene's normals carry the normal maps, so every roof tile and cobble drew a crease line), light_color's strength 0.16 (was 0.22). Every value an estimate until filmed; tune for Kingsmere's square at the default town view.
